tests.prompt: Build a small WordPress plugin that provides a dynamic block named 'wpbp/post-badge'. The block renders a short badge for the post it is placed in: a label, a colon and a space, then the title of the post that the surrounding block context identifies. When the block is rendered with no post in context the title part is the word none instead. The label comes from a 'label' block attribute whose default is 'Post'. Describe the block with block.json metadata and keep the server markup in a separate render file.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: block.json declares name 'wpbp/post-badge', an attributes entry for 'label' (string, default 'Post'), "usesContext": ["postId"], and "render": "file:./render.php". The plugin registers the block from that metadata, so WP_Block_Type::$uses_context contains postId and the render callback is the one synthesized by register_block_type_from_metadata(). Rendering the block with context postId set to two different posts yields the two different post titles; rendering with no context yields 'Post: none'; an explicit label attribute replaces the default. The markup is a single span carrying the class wpbp-post-badge.
requirements: Ship a block.json that declares the block name, its label attribute and default, and the post context the block consumes.
Keep the server-side markup in its own PHP render file referenced from the block metadata rather than an inline render callback.
Render exactly one span element carrying the class wpbp-post-badge whose text is the label, a colon and a space, then the post title.
Register the block when WordPress registers block types.

tests.prompt: Build a small WordPress plugin providing two blocks that work together. 'wpbp/roster' is a container block that carries a team name in a 'team' attribute. 'wpbp/roster-member' renders a single span with the class wpbp-roster-member whose text is 'Team: ' followed by the team name of the roster it sits in, however deeply it is nested inside other blocks. A member block placed outside any roster renders 'Team: unassigned'. Describe both blocks with block.json metadata.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: wpbp/roster declares a 'team' attribute and shares it through providesContext; wpbp/roster-member lists that same context key in usesContext and renders it server-side. Because WP_Block passes its available context down through every descendant, a member nested inside a core/group inside the roster still sees the value. Rendering rosters with two different team names produces two different outputs, and a standalone member falls back to 'unassigned'. The registry must show the parent's providesContext mapping the 'team' attribute onto a key the child consumes, so a solution that smuggles the value through a global or a hard-coded string does not qualify.
requirements: Register both block types from block.json metadata.
Take the team name from the container's 'team' block attribute and share it with descendants through block context.
Render the member block server-side as exactly one span with the class wpbp-roster-member.
Fall back to the word unassigned when no roster context is present.

required_patterns.description: The container shares its attribute as block context
The member block consumes the shared context

tests.prompt: Register a dynamic block type 'wpbp/promo' that opts into wide and full alignment and into background colour, and that stores its copy in a 'text' attribute defaulting to 'Promo'. The block renders as a single div containing the escaped text. That div must carry every class and inline style WordPress derives from the block's supports and attributes for the editor's saved values, and in addition the class 'promo' before any of them plus the attribute data-promo="1".
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: the render callback builds its opening tag with get_block_wrapper_attributes(), passing array( 'class' => 'promo', 'data-promo' => '1' ). Core merges the extra class list before the support-generated one, so 'promo' leads and alignwide, wp-block-wpbp-promo, has-background, has-accent-1-background-color and any className value follow. With no attributes the wrapper carries only 'promo' and the generated wp-block-wpbp-promo class, and no style attribute. A custom background colour yields has-background plus an inline background-color declaration, and never the preset slug class. Hand-assembled class strings or a second class attribute alongside the generated one fail.
requirements: Register the block type when the function is called so the block renders through WordPress.
Declare wide and full alignment support and background colour support on the block type.
Give the block a 'text' attribute of type string that defaults to 'Promo'.
Render exactly one div whose attributes combine the block's own support-derived attributes with the promo class and data-promo="1".

tests.prompt: Given a block document as a string, report the image IDs of the image blocks that sit directly inside a gallery block. An image nested deeper than that - inside a group that is inside the gallery, say - does not count, nor does an image outside any gallery, nor an image block from some other namespace that happens to be named image. Galleries may themselves be nested. Return the ids as integers in the order the blocks appear in the document.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: the containment relationship is the direct parent, so the answer is the block whose enclosing block is core/gallery, at any nesting depth of that gallery. WP_Block_Processor expresses this with get_breadcrumbs(), whose last entry is the matched block itself and whose second-to-last entry is its parent. Delimiters written as wp:image and wp:core/image are the same block type, while wp:wpbp/image is not. Documents with no qualifying image return an empty list.
requirements: Take the block document as a string argument and return a list of integers.
Include an image only when its immediate containing block is a gallery.
Treat a delimiter written with an explicit core namespace as the same block type as one without.
Preserve document order.

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_block_api_015( string $document ): array { $ids = array(); $processor = new WP_Block_Processor( $document ); while ( $processor->next_block( 'core/image' ) ) { $crumbs = $processor->get_breadcrumbs(); $depth = count( $crumbs ); if ( $depth < 2 || 'core/gallery' !== $crumbs[ $depth - 2 ] ) { continue; } $attributes = $processor->allocate_and_return_parsed_attributes(); if ( isset( $attributes['id'] ) ) { $ids[] = (int) $attributes['id']; } } return $ids; }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_block_api_015( string $document ): array { $ids = array(); $processor = new WP_Block_Processor( $document ); while ( $processor->next_block( 'core/image' ) ) { $crumbs = $processor->get_breadcrumbs(); if ( ! in_array( 'core/gallery', $crumbs, true ) ) { continue; } $attributes = $processor->allocate_and_return_parsed_attributes(); if ( isset( $attributes['id'] ) ) { $ids[] = (int) $attributes['id']; } } return $ids; }

function wpbp_block_api_015( string $document ): array { $ids = array(); if ( preg_match_all( '~<!--\\s+wp:(?:core/)?image\\s+(\\{.*?\\})~', $document, $matches ) ) { foreach ( $matches[1] as $json ) { $attributes = json_decode( $json, true ); if ( isset( $attributes['id'] ) ) { $ids[] = (int) $attributes['id']; } } } return $ids; }

tests.prompt: Label the top-level sections of a block document. Given the document's markup as a string, return markup in which every top-level block that has a block type carries the editor block name 'Section N' in its block metadata, numbered from 1 in document order. Blocks nested inside other blocks must not be labelled or otherwise changed, metadata a top-level block already carries must survive alongside the new name, classic content that has no block type is left exactly as it was, and nothing else in the markup may change.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: the label lives in the block's attrs under metadata.name, the attribute the editor's block rename feature uses. traverse_and_serialize_blocks() hands the pre-callback a reference to the block plus its parent, and the parent is null exactly for top-level blocks, which is how nested blocks are skipped while the tree is reserialized. Existing metadata keys such as categories must be merged with, not replaced by, the new name. Classic chunks have a null blockName and must round-trip byte for byte.
requirements: Take the markup as a string and return the rewritten markup.
Number only the top-level blocks that have a block type, starting at 1.
Leave nested blocks and their attributes untouched.
Preserve metadata entries the labelled blocks already carry.

required_patterns.description: Writes the label into block metadata

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_block_api_016( string $document ): string { $index = 0; return traverse_and_serialize_blocks( parse_blocks( $document ), static function ( array &$block, ?array &$parent_block, $previous_block ) use ( &$index ): string { if ( null !== $parent_block ) { return ''; } $name = $block['blockName'] ?? null; if ( ! is_string( $name ) || '' === $name ) { return ''; } ++$index; $metadata = $block['attrs']['metadata'] ?? array(); if ( ! is_array( $metadata ) ) { $metadata = array(); } $metadata['name'] = 'Section ' . $index; $block['attrs']['metadata'] = $metadata; return ''; } ); }
